summary:
MGMT’s fourth album, *Little Dark Age*, was released by Columbia Records on February 9, 2018, ending a gap of more than four years since *MGMT* (2013). It reached No. 35 on the Billboard 200 and received generally favorable reviews, with critics often describing it as a partial return to the pop hooks of *Oracular Spectacular* (2007). Its Metacritic score was 77 from 24 reviews.

Andrew VanWyngarden and Ben Goldwasser regrouped in late 2015 after taking time off. Early sessions stalled until producer Patrick Wimberly helped spur new ideas and encouraged outside collaborators—a first for the band—including Ariel Pink, James Richardson, and Wimberly. Connan Mockasin and Sébastien Tellier also contributed. The duo generated about 40 song ideas, then recorded with Wimberly and longtime producer Dave Fridmann at Tarbox Road Studios in 2016. The 2016 U.S. election shaped the album’s mood; the band aimed to make fun, immediate songs amid a bleak climate.

The title reflects the band’s dismay at political and social events, especially Donald Trump’s election, while suggesting the dark period will end. The cover uses a 1988 illustration by Jim Taber, originally published in a horror and supernatural zine. The gatefold reproduces part of Swiss artist Aloïse Corbaz’s *Nénuphars/Paix Christi*; the liner notes mistakenly name the other side of the drawing.

The album’s four singles were “Little Dark Age,” “When You Die,” “Hand It Over,” and “Me and Michael.” The tour began in Berlin on January 30, 2018, and included appearances at NOS Alive, Splendour in the Grass, and Fuji Rock Festival. Critics praised the album’s hooks and eccentricity, though some found it short on ideas or caught between pop and experimentation.
